data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The sum of all possible values of n is 16592.","counterconditions":[{"case":"There exists a prime p such that p^20 < 12005.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The set of primes q for p=2 or p=3 was incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The calculation of n = m - 2005 was performed incorrectly.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Let m = n + 2005. The number of factors d(m) = 21. Since 21 = 21 * 1 = 7 * 3, the prime factorization of m must be p^20 or p^6 * q^2 for distinct primes p, q. For m = p^20, 2^20 = 1,048,576, which exceeds the upper bound m < 12005 (since n < 10,000). For m = p^6 * q^2: 1) p=2: m = 64q^2. 2006 <= 64q^2 < 12005 implies 31.34 <= q^2 < 187.57. Prime q can be 7, 11, 13. Values for m: 64*49=3136, 64*121=7744, 64*169=10816. 2) p=3: m = 729q^2. 2006 <= 729q^2 < 12005 implies 2.75 <= q^2 < 16.45. Prime q can be 2, 3. Since p!=q, q=2. Value for m: 729*4=2916. 3) p>=5: m >= 5^6 * q^2 = 15625 * q^2, which exceeds 12005. Possible values of m are {2916, 3136, 7744, 10816}. Possible values of n (m - 2005) are {911, 1131, 5739, 8811}. Sum = 911 + 1131 + 5739 + 8811 = 16592.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
